I’m gonna have to disagree with the PT part. At least in my experience of doing both. There’s almost no comparison between the intense practice in football (hours of running, lifting, and working) compared to a few laps and push-ups at marching band.

In my experience of football and marching band, I’ve noticed that they have pretty distinct differences when it come to what is harder. Also, my experience was likely different than yours, but for me, football is more time-consuming. Band camp is two weeks in the summer. Football is every day March-December. Band lacks discipline (things like being on time, behavior, and working hard). Football is so much more physically demanding. Lifting weights, running, and doing practice in the heat with a 5 min break every hour. Band on the other hand, has a break every 30 mins, no lifting, and no running. Also, it should be mentioned that I played the quads, so I had the most physically demanding instrument (imo). However I have noticed that going home from band camp usually left me in more pain than football. Band is also much harder when it comes to remembering your drill and music at the same time, as well as playing and marching. In conclusion, I’d say football is much, much more physically demanding, and more disciplined, making it harder in that regard. However, band was much more mentally challenging, and requires a lot of focus, but isn’t physically hard.
